## Who he is

Roger Federer (born 8 August 1981 in Basel, Switzerland) turned professional in
1998 and retired from competitive tennis in September 2022 at the Laver Cup in
London. Over a 24-year career he won 20 major singles titles, spent a record 237
consecutive weeks ranked World No. 1, and became the first man to win 100 or more
tour-level singles titles in the Open Era after Jimmy Connors.

Beyond the trophies, Federer is remembered for a one-handed backhand, an
efficient all-court game, and a demeanour that made him a global ambassador for
the sport. His rivalries with Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic defined men's
tennis for nearly two decades.
